A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RSA2C and contain readable text, figures, tables, equations, and experimental, algorithmic, and proof appendices. Corresponding content can be matched despite substantial formatting and numbering changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original continuous-control experiments on Pendulum-v1, BipedalWalker-v3, and Ant-v5, plus an LQR convergence simulation.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark and LQR results and additionally reports high-noise tests and dictionary/memory measurements.

M1.justification: The Gaussian RKHS Actor, two Critics, SHAP-weighted kernel, KME/CME attribution routes, two-timescale updates, and ALD sparsification remain unchanged. Added explanations and dictionary-size subscripts do not establish a different algorithm.

E1.justification: The three continuous-control environments and LQR task are retained. v3 modestly extends input-condition coverage to severe observation noise at variances 0.05, 0.1, and 0.5 in Table 9, beyond the previous maximum of 0.01.

E2.justification: v3 adds Uniform SHAP to the ablations in Figures 2, 5, and 8. Its stability comparisons also add Advanced AC, Uniform SHAP, and RKHS-AC alongside the retained RSA2C variants, SAC, and PPO, substantially expanding controls for attribution-related robustness.

E3.justification: v3 adds convergence epochs and time-to-solution in Table 1 and fixed-time-budget memory profiling in Figure 12. The original benchmark hyperparameters and evaluation episode counts remain unchanged. The new solution threshold and profiling time budget are not specified.

E4.justification: New analyses test learned versus uniform attribution, robustness under much stronger noise, and dictionary growth and memory scaling. These substantially expand the diagnostic evidence. The existing LQR optimality-gap analysis is retained, moving from Appendix A.5 to A.6.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over 10 random seeds and use standard deviations and shaded variability bands. Changed uncertainty values and additional result rows do not establish a change in statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: All three benchmark stability tables and several learning curves change. At Pendulum noise 0.001, KME changes from -316.48 ± 225.94 to -147.49 ± 32.40; noiseless Ant SAC changes from 4477.33 ± 1950.69 to 3763.55 ± 972.24. v3 also adds high-noise, memory, and time-to-solution results while removing several kernel-baseline cost entries. The reasons for the revised scores are not documented.

T1.justification: The perturbation bounds, convergence rates, supporting lemmas, and proof arguments are retained. Dictionary-size subscripts, statement numbering, and equation arrangement change without introducing a substantive new mathematical result or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: attribution-guided kernel actor-critic learning, intrinsic interpretability, global non-asymptotic convergence under perturbations, and efficient, stable continuous control.

C2.justification: Section 5 replaces the strong CME-versus-KME robustness contrast with an interpretation of both variants as stable and acknowledges SAC's competitive Pendulum results and fastest time-to-solution. Appendix A.4 reinterprets the unchanged sparse KME attribution plots as stable, task-relevant signals rather than weak explanations. New discussion adds dictionary-memory limitations alongside the retained high-dimensional representation bottleneck.

D1.justification: v3 newly supplies a code-repository link in the abstract. The benchmark hyperparameters, processor description, and Appendix B implementation details are otherwise substantially retained; the link alone does not establish the repository's contents.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to explainable RL, kernel RL, and two-timescale actor-critic research remain unchanged. Reference formatting and an added URL for an existing citation are bibliographic edits.

P1.justification: The experimental discussions in Section 5 and Appendices A.3–A.4 are extensively rewritten. v3 also adds explanatory footnotes, an Additional Results subsection, Limitations, acknowledgements, and an impact statement, and removes the contents list. The main methodological and proof sequence remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column conference layout for the main text, consolidates hyperparameter and computational-cost tables, redraws several learning curves, and expands stability tables. Table 9 and the nine-panel memory Figure 12 are new. The architecture, SHAP visualizations, and LQR plot are retained.

improvement.justification: The added attribution controls and broader noise comparisons strengthen experimental scrutiny, while severe-noise failures, memory limitations, and a code link improve transparency. These gains are limited by unexplained score revisions and weakly specified efficiency comparisons: Table 1 gives Ant PPO 3,491 convergence epochs without reconciling this with the stated 2,000-epoch budget and displayed curve.
